windows.note: English-family TCG products enumerated from Yugipedia set pages (all five English release-date properties) joined with the YGOPRODeck bulk dump; see data/imported/releases-report.json for known gaps.

Japanese OCG products and promotional distributions from the beginning of the OCG (per Yugipedia's own "Series 1" window, 1999-02-01) through the day before the August 26, 1999 Tokyo Dome event, hand-curated (curated:true). 19 products certified (2026-08 recertification; was 20 at the original 2026-08 certification pass, corrected down by 1 - see below); 5 anomalies discovered during research are accounted for in data/releases/gaps.json (gap-ocg1999-*), none unresolved. The December 16, 1998 Duel Monsters (video game 1) collector's cards are deliberately excluded: Yugipedia's own Series 1 sets template classifies them, and the entire Bandai Carddass/Sealdass card lines, as "Non-OCG (1997-1999)", predating the OCG's actual 1999-02 launch. RECERTIFICATION NOTE (2026-08): an independent multi-agent primary-source audit found the original certification pass (i) had wrongly dated two Duel Monsters II Game Guide promo cards by copying an unrelated product's date (corrected: Game Guide 1 1999-07-08->1999-07-13, Game Guide 2 1999-08-05->1999-08-10, both re-verified directly against Konami's own card-level print-history; neither correction crosses the cutoff) and (ii) had fabricated a physical "National Tournament prize cards" release dated 1999-02-21 for three cards (Millennium Shield, Megasonic Eye, Yamadron) that were actually only a Game Boy video-game hidden-card reward, never a physical OCG release - that product record has been deleted. All three cards remain correctly in the certified pool via their genuine 1999-06-01 Limited Edition pack release, so the candidate pool's cardinality and digest are unaffected by any of these corrections; only chronological/provenance accuracy changed. See docs/research/yugi-kaiba-format-source-gate.md "2026-08 recertification" section and tests/fixtures/ocg1999-official-chronology.json for the independently-sourced evidence fixture this recertification is pinned against.

ocg-jp 1999: the Duel Monsters National Tournament prize cards' top-placer tier, the Tokyo Dome invitation Ticket cards, and 3 small redundant promo distributions (V Jump August 1999 Special Present, V Jump Festa 1999, the DM2 trial-meeting card) are accounted for by resolved-safe gap-ocg1999-* records rather than product rosters; see data/releases/gaps.json.
notes: known_gaps above are importer-detected anomaly tallies kept for bookkeeping, NOT unresolved certification failures: certification is governed by the gap ledger (data/releases/gaps.json), and the validator requires every anomaly counted here to be accounted for by a ledger record (unaccounted anomalies fail validation as gaps.unaccounted).
